clinicalDetails.clinicalHistory: Patient was involved in a road traffic accident eight months ago resulting in a left tibial condylar fracture and an avulsion ACL tear. Open reduction and internal fixation was performed by Dr. Hemant Kalyan, followed by 4 to 6 weeks of non-weight bearing and subsequent progressive loading. Despite eight months having passed, the patient has not returned to full functional activity.
clinicalDetails.chiefComplaint: Left knee pain, difficulty performing functional activities and difficulty walking along with ankle and back pain during prolonged walking following surgery

subjectiveAssessments.conclusion: Restricted and painful knee flexion on overpressure
Generally full and pain free although left hip extension was restricted

subjectiveGoals.goalDetails: Return to full functional activity and prolonged walking without pain

objectiveGoals.goalName: Single Leg Stability and Quadriceps Strength

patientAdvice.adviceDetails: Restoring extension, improving stability and single leg stability, strengthening quadriceps and functional lower limb musculature, improving ankle mobility, and activating the posterior chain.
